title: These Ants Farm Fungus With 8 Million Workers and Antibiotics

scenes.text: These ants cut leaves, but they never eat them.
Leafcutter ants haul leaf pieces home, carrying many times their own weight.
They chew the leaves into paste and grow a fungus on it. The fungus is their food.
One nest can hold up to eight million ants.
And the ants carry bacteria that make an antibiotic, to keep mold out of the farm.
Eight million farmers. And not one of them eats a leaf.

description:
Leafcutter ants cut leaves to grow a fungus garden, and they eat the fungus, not the leaves.
One nest can hold up to eight million ants. The ants carry a bacterium that produces an antibiotic protecting their fungus farm from mold.
Which would you rather have: their farm or their strength? Comment below.
first_comment: Their jaws vibrate about 1,000 times a second while cutting a leaf. Would you want that on your farm tools?
